items.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: He was a good friend. ... I miss Buck Clayton because he was a real dear friend of mine.

ctx.x: Interesting that you ended up playing with them. But we’ll get to that. You played with Humphrey Lyttelton? Was he one of the well known jazz people in the United Kingdom?

Yeah. Humphrey Lyttelton, he started off in the traditional jazz field you know, with banjos and stuff like that. And then gradually, over a period of time, gradually, by listening, his hero was always Louis Armstrong and Sidney Bechet. But then he became, his taste became more catholic and he started developing a liking for people like Roy Eldridge and Buck Clayton, and then Buck Clayton became a big friend. You know Buck Clayton used to come over and do a lot of tours with us. Buck Clayton and Jimmy Rushing or…
He should be teaching in a university somewhere.
